title: Evaluation preserved by tree unrolling
statement: Let $F$ be a Boolean layered circuit with input type $	ext{Fin }n$, and assign to each non-input node an AND or OR flag. Suppose every gate has finite arity and computes the conjunction of its inputs when its flag is AND, and their disjunction otherwise. For every layer index $m<	ext{depth}(F)+1$, every node $v$ in that layer, and every Boolean assignment $x$ to the inputs, the tree obtained by recursively unrolling $v$ evaluates to the same Boolean value as $v$ in $F$ under $x$.
hypotheses_covered: $F$ is a Boolean layered circuit with input type $	ext{Fin }n$
An AND-or-OR flag is specified for each gate's output node
Every gate computes the conjunction or disjunction of its inputs according to its flag
$x$ is a Boolean assignment to the inputs
replaced:
Let $F$ be a Boolean feedforward circuit whose inputs are indexed by $\mathrm{Fin}\,n$,
and suppose each of its gates has finite arity and computes either the conjunction or
the disjunction of its inputs, according to a flag marking every non-input node as an
AND node or an OR node. Then for every layer $m$ with $m \le \mathrm{depth}(F)$, every
node $v$ of layer $m$, and every input assignment $x : \mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \bbf_2$, the
Boolean circuit obtained by tree-unrolling $v$, evaluated at $x$, equals the value that
$v$ takes in $F$ under the assignment $x$.
